workload_workday_length_002.answer: 8 hours for most teachers (e.g., K-5 8:00 a.m.–4:00 p.m.; Middle School 8:10 a.m.–4:10 p.m.; High School 7:15 a.m.–3:15 p.m.); variations exist for alternative campuses (AEC, ACE, PAC, GRCTC, Memorial Pathway/Non-Traditional).
workload_workday_length_002.evidence: K-5 Teacher and staff 8:00 a.m. - 4:00 p.m.; Middle School Teacher and staff 8:10 a.m. - 4:10 p.m.; High School Teacher and staff 7:15 a.m. - 3:15 p.m.

workload_prep_guarantee_003.evidence: Each classroom teacher is entitled to at least 450 minutes within each two-week period for instructional preparation

workload_prep_minutes_004.answer: At least 450 minutes per two-week period, with a minimum of 45 minutes within the instructional day.
workload_prep_minutes_004.evidence: Each classroom teacher is entitled to at least 450 minutes within each two-week period for instructional preparation... A planning and preparation period under this section may not be less than 45 minutes within the instructional day.

workload_prep_protected_005.evidence: During a planning and preparation period, a classroom teacher may not be required to participate in any other activity.

workload_lunch_duty_free_006.answer: no. Teachers are entitled to a duty-free lunch of at least 30 minutes, but the district may require them to supervise students during lunch one day a week when no other personnel are available.
workload_lunch_duty_free_006.evidence: Teachers and librarians are entitled to a duty-free lunch period of at least 30 minutes. The district may require teachers to supervise students during lunch one day a week when no other personnel are available.
